The point $P(\frac{3}{4},\frac{\sqrt{7}}{4})$ lies on the unit circle, as shown. What is $\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta ?$
question.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14222207/assets/cd63145c6f0513fe78da148b07064eb725c2de88ded4993dabccc0da173d6583.png)

Any point $(x,y)$ on the unit circle is related to the central angle $\theta $ as follows:

$$
x=\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta 
$$

We're given that $y=\frac{\sqrt{7}}{4}$ at the point $P.$ Therefore, we have

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta =\frac{\sqrt{7}}{4}.
$$

Knowing that $\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta =\frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta },$ we can calculate $\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta :$

$$
\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta =\frac{1}{(\frac{\sqrt{7}}{4})}=\frac{4}{\sqrt{7}}=\frac{4\sqrt{7}}{7}.
$$
